projects.title: Developing a unified vehicle dynamic model for autonomous ground vehicle applications
projects.description: Planning and control algorithms for autonomous cars rely on vehicle models that can estimate the trajectory and motion of the vehicle being operated. In robotics, vehicle motion models have often been developed based on kinematic models. Although they have enjoyed great success in applications such as simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), these basic models have shown to be limiting when applied to planning and control algorithms. This report describes the development of a vehicle model that extends the basic kinematic model of a four-wheeled ground vehicle by incorporating lateral and longitudinal dynamic models. The performance of this model is then presented using real-world datasets.

projects.title: Vehicle Trajectory Smoothing using iSAM and GICP
projects.description: Autonomous cars commonly leverage maps that are built offline for their online operation. To build these maps, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) systems are leveraged. The goal of this project was to implement incremental smoothing and mapping (iSAM) to solve the back-end inference problem and to implement generalized iterative closest point (GICP) to solve the front-end SLAM problem. We present some results using real-world datasets that demonstrate the performance of our solution.
